why: Verifier Check 3 would not run as written. The regex `'^#+\\s*'+n+'\\s*\\('` sits inside a double-quoted `node -e "..."`. Bash turns `\\` into `\`, so JS receives `'\s*'` and `'\('`, which become plain `s*` and `(`. The pattern `^#+s*adds*(` has an unclosed group, so `new RegExp` throws "Invalid regular expression" and the check errors even when the README is correct. The other commands look runnable: Checks 1 and 2 (`node -e`) and `npm test`, whose script is `node --test`. The named files math.js, README.md and test/math.test.js exist. The `!=` in Check 1 is safe from history expansion, and the `!(` in Check 2 only matters in an interactive shell.
